The justification for the study arises from the provisions of the Smart Mobility Strategy (SSMS) COM (2020) 789 and in specific the 2021 New Urban Mobility Framework (UMF) COM (2021) 811. The SMSS calls for EU and Member States to deliver on citizens’ expectations of cleaner air, less noise and congestion through an improved European framework on urban mobility. Urban Vehicle Access Regulations (UVARs) are essential in this context as a means to address issues of local air quality, congestion and noise caused by urban transport. The UMF calls for an uptake on resolving specific UVAR challenges that risk to adversely affect the internal market as concerns the free movement of persons and goods along the TEN-T network and its urban nodes. The study is explicitly referred to under the action box of UMF chapter 2.7. 
Across Europe, there is a variety of UVAR schemes applied and there is no “one size-fits all approach” for such schemes in view of the specific city challenges the scheme is to respond to. The variety of different schemes, its governance, compliance and enforcement modus-operandi thus poses new challenges for passenger and freight transport which in turn affects and limits the effectiveness of measures taken and leads to complaints by road users. In recent years, the Commission has received an increasing number of complaints from European citizens. Especially during UVAR start-up phases, there is a risk that the haphazard implementation of UVARs jeopardizes public acceptance, creates obstacles to free movement of persons and goods under internal market perspectives and to fair and equal treatment of resident and non-residents (discrimination). Increasing UVAR efficiency under user-friendly compliance and information schemes is thus essential, as is the cross-border data exchange of vehicle and driver data, UVAR digitisation etc.
The study mainly builds on the conclusions and recommendation of the UVAR Exchange Project to be completed in Feb 2023 – and others of relevance such as e.g. the UVAR BOX and Civitas-ReVeAL intervention that ended in theth quarter 2022. The purpose is to map and clarify on digital and technical solutions in order to enable more effective and user-friendly UVARs.

normalized.title: Mapping study on digital and technical solutions to enable more effective and user-friendly UVARs, while respecting the principle of subsidiarity
normalized.description:
Please note that this is not a call for tenders but a publication announcing the Contracting authority’s intention to publish a future negotiated low or middle valueprocedure. 
The justification for the study arises from the provisions of the Smart Mobility Strategy (SSMS) COM (2020) 789 and in specific the 2021 New Urban Mobility Framework (UMF) COM (2021) 811. The SMSS calls for EU and Member States to deliver on citizens’ expectations of cleaner air, less noise and congestion through an improved European framework on urban mobility. Urban Vehicle Access Regulations (UVARs) are essential in this context as a means to address issues of local air quality, congestion and noise caused by urban transport. The UMF calls for an uptake on resolving specific UVAR challenges that risk to adversely affect the internal market as concerns the free movement of persons and goods along the TEN-T network and its urban nodes. The study is explicitly referred to under the action box of UMF chapter 2.7. 
Across Europe, there is a variety of UVAR schemes applied and there is no “one size-fits all approach” for such schemes in view of the specific city challenges the scheme is to respond to. The variety of different schemes, its governance, compliance and enforcement modus-operandi thus poses new challenges for passenger and freight transport which in turn affects and limits the effectiveness of measures taken and leads to complaints by road users. In recent years, the Commission has received an increasing number of complaints from European citizens. Especially during UVAR start-up phases, there is a risk that the haphazard implementation of UVARs jeopardizes public acceptance, creates obstacles to free movement of persons and goods under internal market perspectives and to fair and equal treatment of resident and non-residents (discrimination). Increasing UVAR efficiency under user-friendly compliance and information schemes is thus essential, as is the cross-border data exchange of vehicle and driver data, UVAR digitisation etc.
The study mainly builds on the conclusions and recommendation of the UVAR Exchange Project to be completed in Feb 2023 – and others of relevance such as e.g. the UVAR BOX and Civitas-ReVeAL intervention that ended in theth quarter 2022. The purpose is to map and clarify on digital and technical solutions in order to enable more effective and user-friendly UVARs.

Title: Germany – Architectural, construction, engineering and inspection services – BLB NRW Köln / Universität Bonn / Ersatzneubau Pharmazie AVZ II / Baucontrolling KG 400
Procedure title: BLB NRW Köln / Universität Bonn / Ersatzneubau Pharmazie AVZ II / Baucontrolling KG 400
Description: Der Bau- und Liegenschaftsbetrieb NRW, Niederlassung Köln, realisiert den Ersatzneubau des Pharmazeutischen Instituts (AVZ II) für die Rheinische Friedrich-Wilhelms-Universität Bonn am Campus Endenich. Mit dem Neubau werden die Fachgruppen Pharmazie in einem zeitgemäßen Gebäude zusammengeführt, das optimale Bedingungen für Studierende und Mitarbeitende bietet. Die vorbereitenden Maßnahmen zu Infrastruktur und Freianlagen übernimmt der BLB. Gegenstand dieses VgV-Vergabeverfahrens sind die erforderlichen Leistungen des Baucontrolling der KG400 zur Leistungsüberwachung eines Generalunternehmers ab Leistungsphase 5.
Lot description: Der Neubau umfasst Laborflächen der Sicherheitsstufen S1 und S2, Praktikumsräume, Büros, Hörsäle, Seminarräume sowie eine Cafeteria mit Essensausgabe für rund 2.000 Studierende. Die Nutzungsfläche beträgt ca. 7.100 m2 und die BGF ca. 16.000 m2. Das Gebäude wird ganzjährig genutzt und bietet Platz für bis zu 400 Studierende und 130 Mitarbeitende gleichzeitig. Die Planung sieht flexible und fakultätsübergreifende Nutzung der Flächen und Geräte vor, um Synergieeffekte zu erzielen. Die technische Gebäudeausrüstung wird gemäß den Anforderungsprofilen der Universität umgesetzt. Ab Leistungsphase 5 übernimmt ein Generalunternehmer die Ausführungsplanung und Bauleistungen. Im Zuge dessen wird das Baucontrolling der technischen Gebäudeausrüstung (KG400) eingerichtet, um die Umsetzung der technischen Anforderungen und Standards der Universität Bonn zu begleiten und zu überwachen. Das Baucontrolling unterstützt die Qualitätssicherung, prüft technische Lösungen und Alternativen und bewertet deren Auswirkungen auf Kosten, Termine und Qualitäten. Darüber hinaus wirkt das Baucontrolling im Entscheidungsprozess mit und begleitet die Projektbesprechungen im Rahmen der Bauausführung. Weitere Details zum Objekt sowie für die gesamte Leistungserbringung sind darüber hinaus den weiteren Projektunterlagen zu entnehmen. Dazu gehören insbesondere Projektstandards, anonymisierte Pläne, die Funktionale Leistungsbeschreibung (FLB) sowie eine detaillierte Schnittstellenliste.

The developed IP shall be able to solve complex FFT / inverse FFT; convolve and correlate vectors in frequency domain, with a length up to 32768 points, gain and phase correction, filtering, etc. Several applications will benefit from such an IP Core: - Active Microwave Remote Sensing: Radar Onboard Processing, such as SAR Image Formation, RFI Detection, Compression - Passive Microwave Remote Sensing: Hyperspectral Radiometers (channelisation, RFI detection), Compression Although FFT IPs are available commercially, fine spectral resolution together with high sampling rate (e.g. direct conversion) leads to long FFT lengths, which may not be available in commercial IPs.
